I am the guardian of feline kind.
I ensure the survival of cats. For this service, Icthlarin grants me eternal life. [...] I look after my kind. For that, Icthlarin looks after me.

She is normally too wrapped up in preserving her immortality to be making conversation. [...] because her immortality is based on the fact that she keeps us cats safe. Her whole existence is dedicated to protecting us.
I am an agent of neither good nor evil. I am unconcerned with the plight of mankind and their petty wars and beliefs. [...] As I've said before, I have no interest in humans and their gods
Well, that went horribly wrong. So this year, I thought to myself, Harvey, how are you going to deliver goodies to all the kids?
name: harvey

quote: All of Gielinor deserve to celebrate Easter. I figured Varrock is a particularly busy place. By positioning myself here I maximise my CTPOTR. Chocolate to person over time ratio. You need to maximise your reach and minimise time spent, to optimise value.
Oh yes, my mother was one. And my father. And their parents before them.
That's the spirit! You know the drill, head down the rabbit hole and speak to my son, he's got a plan that likely requires him to do very little, and you... Well, you'll do it all!
Ahem... secondly, find the toy room in the warrens below, you'll find yourself Milkee, my brother.
Some call me 'Eggrabbit'. Others call me 'Long Ears Johnson'. Many times have I walked past Varrock West Bank and been called 'Sellin lobbies 200gp'.

We are the spirits of the river Elid, many ages ago we used to be mindless wandering spirits, with little mind or purpose, we were here even in the first age. Then great Elidinis came to the desert and bound us to her river, we've become one with the river and over the centuries become full of the power of Elidinis that was in her river. We are now her trusted guardians of the Elid, we can control the river and anything which happens near the river we know about.

quote: Be careful in there, there are still some of those baby Tanglefootii around.
Large parts of the book are written using the vampyric language which isn't easy to translate.
First of all they were looking for a way to increase the amount of blood that can be harvested from a human.

As we're already aware, vampyres possess some form of immunity against our attacks. It starts off as only partial in juveniles and juvinates but by the time they become vyres they are totally invulnerable. This book implies that the vampyres immunity isn't perfect and that it can be overcome. It seems they were trying to improve this immunity.
The only thing I have of [my great-grandfather] is a key. It's a strange key, it changes temperature by itself as you walk around. I'm afraid I don't know what it's for, though.

They're not followers, they're slaves, they're the soulless... (What happened to them?) They were normal once, adventurers, treasure hunters. But men are weak, they couldn't ignore the voices. Now they all seem to think with one conscience... As if they're being controlled by one being... (Iban?) Maybe... maybe Zamorak himself. Those who try and fight it are locked in cages, until their minds are too weak to resist.

It is the White Tree, last survivor of a race of Trees that have disappeared from our landscape. Once they covered the land; now there is only one. [What happened to them?] Man desired the wood of the White Tree, because of its wood of pure white. Need I tell you more?
I work for a business known as Sandy Sand Co.

Being so close to the shore, Rellekka provides a lot of seaweed alongside my sand... the seaweed from Rellekka, in combination with my sand business, provides a huge amount of glass for the surrounding areas! Fellow Fremenniks aren't too pleased with my outside dealings, though know how important my job is. I think they let it slide for that reason.
No, I hardly knew him. He was meant to tell me how to get out of Menaphos; now that he's dead, I'm stuck here.

It was about the same time the passage to the surface opened up. I was visiting Juna, the Story-Snake. She likes to hear of my adventures and she sometimes lets me drink the Tears of Guthix. Zanik: ...And when they opened up the giant frog's stomach they found all the missing silver, and Mistag's brooch!
Although their god was gone, many Zarosians fought to keep his empire alive.

She [Nex] was Zaros' most powerful weapon, and she led a great army to try and restore his empire. Not that she needed an army of course. Nex alone was powerful enough to hold back hundreds of lesser beings.
The forces of Saradomin knew that Nex needed to be dealt with. They were able to lure her into these caverns.
After great effort and sacrifice, they managed to place Nex and her followers into a frozen, enchanted sleep.
Once Nex was no longer an immediate threat, they built the Temple of Lost Ancients around her. Most of the temple has since fallen to ruin, but you can still see some of the remains.
Later in the war, a great battle broke out in the Temple of Lost Ancients. I was a Saradominist soldier at the time, and I was among those who fought for him in that battle.
...many of us had grown tired of war. One of our priests discovered this. He came to us and revealed that he felt the same way, and that he had secretly converted to Guthix.
He encouraged us to join him. We abandoned the cause of Saradomin and became followers of Guthix.
Our new leader taught us the ways of the druids, including an ancient ritual that had the power to awaken Guthix himself. We believed this ritual to be the only way to end the war.
When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. The ritual also destroyed the protective enchantments on their prison.
I never saw him [the priest] again. He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him... I heard little of what they said, but I did hear what she called him. Sliske.
Nex posed such a danger, that the four armies temorarily joined forces to drive her back into the prison. They resealed it, but were unable to fix the enchantments we destroyed.
Devin Mendelberg comes from some town in Morytania - ghastly place! I'm not surprised he moved about as far west as he could go! He helps Franklin with the machinery, among other things.
Ramara's another Ardougnian. Her father's a baker there, but she didn't want to spend her whole life baking and doing his accounts.
That's alright. My name is Louisiana Jones, although most people call me Anna. I'm an archaeologist.
Hah! No, I used to, but now I prefer to work freelance for independent employers.
I can say that I can't say anything about what you want me to say!

I'm investigating the relative co-existence of convergent entries from two para-dimensional spaces into a quantum metaphysical universe and exponential decay of said pathways in the event of fluctuations in the space-time cortex.
Ivan is the last living descendant of Ivandis Seergaze himself. Once I am gone, he will be the only remaining descendant of the Seven Priestly Warriors.
These mines are actually the territory of one of the eight major companies of the mining Consortium.
Stepmother? Ho! Good lord, no. No king in his right mind would marry a hag like that!No, this is her evil second-cousin, twice-removed.

Well, you know that this time of year Santa travels the multiverse, judging children and adults alike for their behaviour and rewarding them accordingly?

Alas, that was a long time ago. I've since passed away. (...) Oh we all are here! Santa gave us the opportunity to stay here in this sanctuary. (...) That's just the thing, while we are in here we can keep our mortal body with Santa's magic.
name: undead

quote: Several weeks ago, a dwarven explorer, named Nestor Peregrine, discovered the entrance to an ancient cave complex while exploring the troll mountains. On his return to Keldagrim, he celebrated in a tavern where we have an informant. The dwarf spoke of a great treasure, apparently mentioned in dwarven legend, and of creatures of great evil, fighting those of great good. I sent Sir Gerry and a small command of knights to investigate the dwarf's stories several months ago and it appears that he has found the resting place of that incredible weapon: the Godsword.
So I went to Cook, the cook at the Blue Moon Inn, to see if I could talk him into giving some leftovers to a potential dog...
Oh, he's right over there... used to work in the mines to the south, poor lad. Made a bit of a mess of things I believe.
[Player: You pirates are nothing but trouble! Why, once I travelled to Lunar Isle with a bunch of your type, and spent days sailing around in circles!] Then ye must know me brother! Murky Pat!
I'm Jeffery, the taskmaster for the Wilderness Achievement Diary.
We need a lot of coal to keep our steam engines going, you know.
[Can I do a bit of mining there as well?] I'm not sure, but as long as no one notices I don't think anyone is going to care.
We haul all our goods to the city by ship, you see.
Molten snow, you see.
But this water here, you see, it comes dripping down from above.
No fish around here.

Really? That's the nicest thing anyone has ever said. I admire him a great deal. He works so hard for this town. ... Hmm, I don't think I do. ... Well, I haven't spoken to him in a while. I don't get out much. ... Maybe the Mayor has finally seen how much I admire him and has grown to admire me? ... Hey, I resent that!

You know, you sound just like the mayor? ... You look like him as well? ... I can see why ... No really, what with the unhealthy skin tone and bulging eyes. The resemblance is uncanny. ... Anything's possible I suppose. Wait a minute, you mean you've always looked that odd?
What do those bureaucratic fools in Menaphos expect! If they're going to take so long to send us a new priestess of She. Do you know we haven't had one for five years now!
They stole a suit of armour when they first broke in months ago, but they've been back four more times since then and taken nothing.
Up to now, our attempts to recover this scroll have been met with disappointment.
Crop circle? Oh, you mean the Puromantic portal?
My employer tells me it is an uncommon sort of tree called the Fyburglars tree.
Made from the wood of the Fyburglars tree, strong and light weight!

We used to be in Seers' Village, far to the west, but we had to move - the seers were complaining about the noise level, and the knights of Camelot got it into their heads that the Party Room knights were making fun of them.
I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres
Oh, thank Armadyl! I am in such a worry... please help me!
Kharrim the messenger... Well, he was always a devoted follower of old General Zamorak, and if I remember rightly Zamorak set up a small base in an old temple near Dareeyak...
Cerberus lives in her chamber linked to Taverley dungeon. She attacks with all combat styles so be prepared.
Oh yes, as I was saying, it was difficult to make a decent living here. I'm afraid this garden was rather neglected during that time.
No, but I do recommend you pick up Kaleef's dagger. I can assure you, it packs some punch.
No, I hardly knew him. He was meant to tell me how to get out of Menaphos; now that he's dead, I'm stuck here.
I'd say so; It managed to pierce that bug's shell.

It has the image of a pegasus on it.
[The Varrock Herald] is edited, printed and published by myself, Benny Gutenberg.
The note says you have committed many sins and atrocities in your life. I'm impressed; I will use you.

The five houses of Kourend each have their own leader who rules over their city. The leaders of the individual houses must enforce and obey the laws set out by the Kourend Council, but can otherwise rule as they see fit.
Hosidius and Shayzien were the two cities founded during the Dragonkin Conflicts.
Most of our history was lost during Xeric's reign.
The Tower was constructed by King Rada III. We don't know exactly when, since dates were not recorded before the Twill Accord.
I know of the powerful magic that keeps them [the creatures] bound below [within the Catacombs].
In the 13th decade, King Shayzien III seized control of Kourend using the military under his command.
[The son of King Shayzien VI] took the name King Hosidius IV in an attempt to distance the family from the breaking of the Royal Accord of Twill.
Alas, according to records, the party never returned and were declared to have perished in the field.

This [Unstable Altar], it seems to give off the same power as the Dark Altar. I believe this altar was created to amplify the power of the Dark Altar, allowing it to reach areas it previously couldn't.
'Quidamortem's creatures are compatible. The experimentation is proving successful and we will soon be ready to mass produce.'
During the battle, the temple surrounding the Dark Altar was destroyed, weakening Xeric's power.
The Royal Guard was established by King Byrne I. He felt that it was dangerous for Shayzien House to control the only military in the kingdom, so he decided to establish a small one of his own.
Well at one time only citizens of Shayzien could join the army. It wasn't until the reign of King Byrne I that people from other parts of the kingdom were allowed to enlist.
It was a thousand years ago, during the time of King Byrne II. I went to my people and shared the secrets of immortality with them.
They came to us. Two of them. The brother and the husband. Her time was running out. They wanted to give her more.
Not all of [Arceuus] accepted this gift of course, as was their right. Those that did, were granted new bodies to house their souls. These bodies are sustained by the Dark Altar.
Forthos was the seat of the Hosidius family before it was destroyed in the War of the Five Houses.
Apparently they [Arceuus] didn't even properly fight in the War of the Five Houses. Still, I guess 'War of the Four Houses while House Arceuus watched' isn't as catchy a name.

He had the servants open a barrel of his finest Aldarin red. Then, he made a toast, to the royal family of Kourend... The entire royal family collapsed before the emperor who looked on with a smile on his face.
From today, the sun will shine on our two kingdoms once more. The mistakes of the past are now behind us.
[The King is] keen to put an end to the animosity between the two kingdoms. Rumor has it [Queen Zyanyi Arkan] feels the same way.
[King Kharedst] married late and his wife... Unfortunately didn't survive bringing Rose into this world.
Are you saying the man I sold those trinkets to was the king?! Those were dark objects, corrupted with powerful magic. Dark magic.
The flask was cursed. Some dark magic. He stopped being himself. Started saying things. Things he would do to people. To the citizens!
There was an Arceuus mage. He was an expert in curses, and he realised what was happening. He gave us the poison for the King.
By then, it was already too late. The King had deteriorated too much. There was only one solution.
Kourend's last King, Kharedst IV, had only one child when he died. She was too young to take the throne, so the Kourend Council was formed to look after things until she came of age.
We didn't want to kill her. She didn't deserve that. The mage gave us a potion. He said it would stop her revealing the truth.
I did some research while you were gone. [Councillor Orson] wasn't lying. The poison they gave [Rose] irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure.
Alas, she was very close to her father and his sudden death drove her to insanity.
After what happened, public life was no place for her. The Council arranged for her to move away so she could escape all of that.
With no suitable ruler, the Kourend Council was made permanent.
[What makes you say the Council have done a bad job?] More crime. Fewer homes. More illness. Loss of jobs. The list goes on.

You know that smell in Port Piscarilius? Imagine that but ten times worse. That's what it was like before the Council had a new sewage system installed. The entire kingdom is now cleaner and safer because of them.
It was under [the Council] that trade with your lands to the east was established. Without those trade routes, you would have no easy way of getting here.

After the last King died, they [the Council] were only supposed to rule until his daughter came of age. However, according to the Council, the King's daughter went mad. Such a wonderful convenience for them of course.
The Council is supposedly voted on by the people every four years. However, the seats have been held by the same four people since the Council was founded.
Ah, so you're the adventurer who's been cooking up a storm around here. Well you'll be pleased to know your hard work was all for nothing. Councillor Hughes has escaped. Lucky her.
I hear the Kourend Royal Guard are leading the investigation. Commander Lydia Fullore is their leader.
You have betrayed the trust of Yama, Sophia Hughes. You have used his generosity to your own advantage. For this, your life is forfeit.
You'd think they'd have some loyalty after all we did! After what we did to him. After what we did to his girl! We were in it together until it no longer suited them!
Martin. He's leader of Kourend's Royal Society. He knows more about the last royal family than anyone. If anyone can help you find Rose, it's him.

Councillor Andrews isn't happy. This is the first time I've directly asked him to perform a task for me. Still, he soon calmed down after a little reminder of who gave him the throne. After all, he wouldn't want the others finding out he was in on it from the start.

[David] placed the device right next to the Altar, just as requested. That said, I likely won't have long to acquire and store the energy needed. The device will no doubt interfere with the ascended humans of Arceuus. They will soon realise something is amiss.

The poison they gave her irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure. Someone else could make the potions, but all they do is prolong her suffering. This is no life for anyone. The truth is, Rose died long ago. All that's left now is an empty shell.
The people should have a say. Anything we decide here should not be finalised until the people have voted on it.

My friends, thank you for putting your trust in me. This kingdom has suffered through much of late, but now it is time for that suffering to end. In honour of her sacrifice, I name this declaration Rose's Accord. With it, the Kingdom of Great Kourend will no longer be a kingdom divided.

We, the leaders of the five houses of Great Kourend, declare that the Kourend Council is no longer fit to rule. As such, you are relieved of your positions with immediate effect. Furthermore, you will both hand yourselves over to Lord Shayzien's soldiers. They will take you into custody where you will await your trial for the crimes of murder and high treason. Along with the now-deceased Liam Orson and Sophia Hughes, the two of you successfully conspired to murder King Kharedst IV and Crown Princess Rose.
The King's late father asked for an advisor from Arceuus. He was keen for us to have a more central role than we did under the Council.

When the people voted on Rose's Accord, they voted for the Hosidius family to become the new royal family. From a technical standpoint that means they voted for King Artur. My job is to advise King Artur and ensure his actions have a positive impact on the people that he now rules.
...the date convention in Great Kourend is to state the number of days and decades since the signing of the Royal Accord of Twill.
Very little is known about those ancient times [before the signing of the Accord], but we refer to such times as decades 'Before Accord', or 'BA' for short.
...as this is the Historical Archive, we stick to the dates used historically within Kourend.
Saradomin is popular with many uneducated citizens of Kourend.
I am a travelling monk from the distant land of Varlamore... I worship Ralos, a common practice where I am from.
While the gods are useful for tedious matters such as granting prayers during combat, we of Arceuus have long moved beyond the need to pay them homage.
This is a place of meditation, where a novice may contemplate the mysteries of the Dark Altar - without venturing too close to its power.
...you may use our church to worship any god you prefer. That would be an ecumenical matter.
I've come to Kourend in search of luck, [player name]. I seek many fortunes and as you know you need luck to find fortune!
Ah these robes keeps me holy, I must remain holy when praying to the God of Luck
Arengeesus, God of luck. We do not know much about her or where she comes from, we just know she is there looking over us.
Those who praise Arengeesus enough to get her attention are rewarded. She will gaze down upon you providing you with luck on your adventures.
[Hard work is all you need.] Perhaps working hard is merely a form of praise to the God of luck, [player name].
There are many souls that find themselves trapped here after death. My people and I do our best to release them.
It was under [the Council] that trade with your lands to the east was established. Without those trade routes, you would have no easy way of getting here.

...we did manage to search his [Xamphur's] lair in Molch. Most of it had been cleared out before we arrived. There was some research left behind though. Notes on potential new spells. Some are far too dangerous to use, but others we've found to be safe. We're preparing a tome of all the ones that are suitable.
The Grand Library of Great Kourend has verified and collated the following extracts from various historical texts
Our people also serves an important role in the wider world. We work to free trapped souls so that they may pass on to the next world. It is a crucial task that the Dark Altar helps us to perform.

Within [Mount Karuulm] live the Tasakaal, three ancient beings with power over life and death. They granted my father the knowledge that led to the Ascent of Arceuus. (...) Their knowledge of the Dark Altar far exceeds ours.
Our forebears spent their lives - literally, in some cases - learning to unlock its secrets and wield its power.
The power of the Dark Altar, reflected in these great crystals, can twist dimensions, warp minds, and even bridge the gulf between life and death.
The Dark Altar powers the Doors of Dinh.

Rejoice! Our mission has succeeded, the Beast has been contained! The Bruma tree burns bright in the night sky, warming the northern tundra and holding back the Beast.
It's not much, but it's enough for that Wintertodt to be able to draw some power into the prison. Probably why them fiery lot have had so much trouble recently.

Well, lacking any sluglings in the area, we add these little grubs called Sweetgrubs. If you ignore the gag- inducing aftertaste, they are quite sweet.
Reality as you know it has many layers, all slightly different with their own rules. Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.

Indeed, there is some relationship between the Kalphite Queen and the desert god Scabaras, but no one is really sure what. During the early part of the fourth age, Scabaras proclaimed himself omnipotent and outlawed worship of all other gods save him. When the people eventually revolted against his repressive rule and banished Scabaras, it is said his blood washed over the scarabs and transformed them into the kalphites we know today. Of course, any right-minded scientist discounts these myths as mere stories, with no historical basis in fact.

We discovered a stash of them in some of our investigations. As far as we have been able to determine, it was created by worshippers of Elidinis in order to smite the followers of Scabaras. They are specially enchanted against both scarab creatures and kalphites...which is odd, since we thought the two races to be entirely different.
name: os

quote: Not really; there are simply details of Scabaras' fall from grace that are only known to we priests. Some of his supposed faults can be forgiven. I just can't explain why at the moment.

Yes, the followers of Scabaras used to be great architects of the subterranean. According to legend, they once planned to build a passage under the river Elid. No doubt Elidinis smote them because none of the followers were ever seen again.
Hah! Those insane earth burrowers! They got their comeuppance! They thought they could undermine the mighty Elidinis so she buried them. They have never been seen around here since.
Annakarl fell early in the war to forces of Saradomin. Attempts to reclaim the fortress have so far been unsuccessful.
Last Known Location [of Zilyana]: Annakarl
Last Known Location [of Lamistard]: Annakarl
He is the very incarnation of health in both mind and body. He is quite popular amongst our soldiers as a result. [...] Our greatest memory masters and orators also tend to follow Het.
Het is the lesser deity concerned with mental and physical health. Sophanem is the city of the dead so Het isn't really worshipped much here.
As you can imagine, the services can be home to some strenuous discussions. [...] They really couldn't decide whether it was a punishment from Het or a curse and an affront to Het.
Hugi, my parents named me that, it means "personification of thought" in the ancient dwarvish tongue.
Well, he does have a relative who wanders all over Gielinor. Comes back from time to time to buy more kebabs. Don't see him very often though.
[Can I have some beer please?] Go to the bar downstairs. I only deal with residents. [Residents? People live here?] No, just guests that stay the night.
[Well what are you interested in stealing?] The heart of a lovely raccoon called Rodney.
The ritual, there were some... adverse effects... [Player: The ritual?] Oh yes! Pretty basic really, head of an Ox, bruma roots, lots of fire and of course the human sacrifice.
You're right with that one [laddie/lass]. Someone or something has made a small hole in the Doors.
It's not much, but it's enough for that Wintertodt to be able to draw some power into the prison. Probably why them fiery lot have had so much trouble recently.

[Player: Does this mean the Wintertodt won't be a threat anymore?] That should be the case in the long run. I suspect it will take a long time though. The Doors were damaged for a while and the Wintertodt will have gained a lot of power. I reckon that magic lot will have to do their fiery tricks for a bit longer before everything is back to normal.
By the way, Lord Zamorak's chaotic power is quite volatile. You'll likely get a smaller harvest from your vine if you're using these blessings.
I was there when Kharedst the Builder opened Kourend Castle
Call me Astra! Now, I must see to this discovery as it may indeed help my mission. May the light shine upon you!
I'm afraid not. We need all of our milk to sell to market, but you can milk the cow yourself if you need the milk.
Tee hee! You've never milked a cow before, have you?
They're operating there under the name of the VTAM Corporation. Be careful. The Phoenixes ain't the types to be messed about.
Hey! You can't go in there. Only authorised personnel of the VTAM Corporation are allowed beyond this point.
Kharrim the messenger... Well, he was always a devoted follower of old General Zamorak, and if I remember rightly Zamorak set up a small base in an old temple near Dareeyak...
Dareeyak is a low priority target for enemy forces. Consider taking advantage of this.
It's choking me up right here, you're making me cry, but hey, I's godda do my job or da kids don't get fed!
Some adventurer had an accident with an alchemy spell... I don't want to talk about it.
A large Bandosian force is marching on Paddewwa. Reinforcements will be needed there.
Graardor and his forces are marching on Paddewwa.
Ah, the evil swordsman Viggora... Paddewwa was where he fought many battles, perhaps he has returned to one of his old haunts?
Before the God Wars, a settlement of the old empire was found here.
The fortress to the east is all that remains on the surface, but there is much still hidden below.
We're blind here. My senses do nothing this close to the ritual marker.
A great prison, sealed long ago.
But to risk unleashing an abomination of the Fallen Empire when the ritual is so close would not be wise.
Hallowvale was taken over by my kind, and Lowerniel became ruler of the newly named Morytania.

Queen Efaritay was a renowned botanist. She used this to her advantage many times during the war, breeding all kinds of plant life to use against us. One of these plants was the Blisterwood tree. The icyene used the sap of this tree to create poisons that were deadly to vampyres.
No one can go in the Arboretum, by order of the Drakan family themselves.

The [Justiciar of the Unicorn] said he was going to confront these [vampyres] but that I should stay to protect the secrets within [the Hallowed Sepulchre]... I carried out my duties though. As we progressed further, we became more experienced at creating the traps. Each one was more deadly than the last. Eventually, when our work was done, I performed the last rites for each of my followers and sealed them within the coffins on the final floor.

Before they were driven out by the vampyres, the Saradominists used their magic to safeguard this place. The dead here were buried with the wealth they had in life. To protect these riches, the Saradominists enchanted the statues within the Sepulchre to create various defences.
Every day that goes by, the number of humans in Morytania decreases. Yet while this happens, our population continues to grow. Unsurprisingly, we no longer have enough blood to go around.

You have been gone too long, brother. While you spend your days hidden away, lamenting about that stupid rock, our kind suffer. Out there, in your city, they're starving. There's not enough blood to go around and their great leader is unwilling to provide a solution. Something has to change, or we're doomed.
Tell me, Vanescula. What is the cause of this latest betrayal? ...This veil of lies is thinner than the humans you feast upon. Now, the truth.

He's a demon of some sorts, but he doesn't seem to have any actual presence in Kourend yet. In fact, until recently, he had no connection to the cult. It does sound odd, but back then they were known as the Disciples of Chaos. They were just a small Zamorakian cult of little note.
The ritual, there were some... adverse effects... [Player: The ritual?] Oh yes! Pretty basic really, head of an Ox, bruma roots, lots of fire and of course the human sacrifice.
I'm no ghost! I'm a spirit, I'm injecting my thoughts into your head

TzHaar are born from eggs incubated in lava pools. When hatched, we retain memories. Memories and knowledge passed on from ancestors who returned to the lava. When TzHaar hatch, some memories are lost. Those about earliest ancestors are not retained. We experiment. [...] We increased the depth at which eggs are incubated. Over time, newly hatched TzHaar had more memories of lost history!
But we kept pushing. We wanted answers, but we went too deep.
Eventually the pool collapsed into a sinkhole. At the bottom we found some sort of ancient incubation chamber, from before earliest memories. We now call it the Inferno.
We decide to experiment more. We take eggs from creatures in Fight Cave and incubate them down there.
When eggs hatched, we see that it was not good decision. They were bigger and stronger, and fought each other for dominance.
All we know is that TzKal-Zuk is hungry. Hungry for memories, memories beyond the Inferno. We think his goal is the city itself. Lots of TzHaar memories here for him.
Deep in inferno, many offspring of TzTok-Jad [...] need dealing with. A challenge for you perhaps, if you're brave enough.
We fear he can't be defeated, but maybe we can hold back his creatures and keep city safe. Player: Well I definitely think I can help with that.
No! TzKal-Zuk's prison is breaking down. There's nothing I can do for you now, JalYt!
A client of mine, a merchant of some repute, is having a sorbet.
Go to the bar downstairs. I only deal with residents. [Residents? People live here?] No, just guests that stay the night.
Zyanyi Arkan, the Sun Queen. She's the ruler of Varlamore, the kingdom in the south.
I am a travelling monk from the distant land of Varlamore... I worship Ralos, a common practice where I am from.
The sun plays an important role in Varlamorian life. In fact, they worship it!
It [soul tranference] was their final attempt to overcome their extinction, but they failed. What you see around you is the result of their failure. It's known as the Strangler.
It's some sort of parasite. It was presumably meant to play a role in their transference rituals, but instead it destroyed them. It has remained here ever since.
When it comes to the existence of Varlamore, it is Xeric we have to thank. During his Age of Strife, many refugees fled Kourend over the previously unexplored Custodia Mountains.
The Varlamorians won't mention this, but we were the first to settle here. Our ancestors saw the writing on the wall when Xeric came to power in Kourend. They chose not to stick around.
Finally we have the dwarves. These were refugees from Lovakengj who established a home beneath Ralos' Rise, becoming known as the Dwarves of Cam Torum.
While they initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.
The next group were the Pericans. They first settled right here, building the town of Fortis, or Civitas illa Fortis as it eventually became.
The dwarves, just as they do today, mostly kept to themselves. However, the Talkasti and Pericans came into regular conflict over various matters.

Long before leaving Kourend, the Talkasti had taken to secretly worshipping Ralos and Ranul. After arriving here, they were able to openly practice their religion for the first time. Over time, the Pericans started to adopt this religion as well.
As the two groups came together, the population of the region started to rapidly expand. This eventually led to the construction of Tempestus, and with it, the founding of Varlamore.
The name comes from the River Varla that separated Talkasti and Perican territory. What was once a symbol of our divide, became the symbol of our unification.

It all started around 100 years ago when Imafore Tullus ascended to the throne. He soon reorganised the kingdom into the Varlamorian Empire, a controversial choice to say the least, though it soon became clear that controversial choices were quite popular with Imafore.
While public opinion was always mixed, nothing he did resulted in outright conflict until his sudden and brutal murder of the Kourend Royal Family.

He had the servants open a barrel of his finest Aldarin red. Then, he made a toast, to the royal family of Kourend... The entire royal family collapsed before the emperor who looked on with a smile on his face.
To say the war was unpopular would be an understatement. Imafore soon found himself facing as much resistance from within as he did from Kourend.
After his death, Imafore was succeeded by King Mezpah Arkan. One of his first acts was to call for the beheading of every statue of Imafore in the kingdom.
The statues remain to this day. It's actually a crime to try and remove them. They exist as a reminder of our history, and a warning to any who would try to follow in Imafore's footsteps.
We have the original Royal Accord of Twill safely stored here. Although it's not available for public viewing, there are copies available within the Grand Library.
From today, the sun will shine on our two kingdoms once more. The mistakes of the past are now behind us.
[The King is] keen to put an end to the animosity between the two kingdoms. Rumor has it [Queen Zyanyi Arkan] feels the same way.
Members of the College are some of the only people allowed to travel to and from Varlamore.
We would often send our students on trips to the east prior to the opening of the borders. The amount of paperwork needed was astounding! Now we can just hop on a ship any time we like!
After all these years, they're finally opening up the kingdom for travel and trade!

King Mezpah set to work on transforming the kingdom. His ambitions were high, to the point that much of what he desired never came to pass in his lifetime. One of his most notable goals was to see Varlamore open more widely to the outer world.
[Teokan] means High Priest
Whereas in other parts of the world you'll likely find followers of many gods, here in Varlamore, you'll only really find those dedicated to Ralos and Ranul.
...most people focus their worship on one of the two, with Ralos being by far the more popular.
Something that is easily forgotten is that while Ranul is indeed a god of death, he is also a god of learning and knowledge.
The Royal Accord of Twill was signed by the rulers of each of the houses 139 decades ago, following the great famine.
Following the rebellion of the five houses against King Rada III, the Council of Elders was formed. They used the Tower as a meeting place for the Council.
note: While it is not stated explicitly who initially joined this council, on the basis of the Eathram & Rada extract, it could be expected to have included the lords united under Eathram, that are mentioned by name in the narration.

quote: The Accord declared that each house will, in turn, rule the Kingdom of Great Kourend for one decade in rotation, based on lots drawn.
Help us fill our Library of Knowledge. In return, we will grant you access to the guild and you will reap the rewards within.
They [the Sect] quickly established this guild with information preservation as their core goal, for men are recorders of history and magic is key for this to last.

As time passes, that which was once fact, becomes myth. Some tales are just that, tales. However, some tales are something more. Here at the Myths' Guild, we live to tell the difference between the two. If you wish to join us, you must do the same.

The story my father told me was of a war on magic. Of god fearing men who believed nothing good would come of wielding a power that was never meant for them. And so the rune temples that man had created were under threat. Before long, all were destroyed and thus forgotten. But the wrath that these Gunnites embraced rippled through the pocket dimensions. Supposedly, a new altar of power was discovered.
...the Sect of Uhld had used the information gained from the wrath altar, and with a spell of their own making, they destroyed the southern runecrafting crusade with much ease.

And so the rune temples that man had created were under threat, all were destroyed and thus forgotten, but the wrath that these Gunnites embraced rippled through the pocket dimensions and a new altar of power was discovered.
The temple [of Wrath] was destroyed just as construction had finished.
...a nearby nomadic group called the Sect of Uhld were not pleased with the brutality they witnessed. Quickly they established this guild with information preservation as their core goal.
...the Sect of Uhld had used the information gained from the wrath altar, and with a spell of their own making, they destroyed the southern runecrafting crusade with much ease.

Camorra came from the town of Saranthium and sat next to the one with a crossbow. The one from Zartharim sat at the north of the table, opposite the one with the sword. The one with an axe asked the one to their right what the journey from Karville was like. Suddenly, Aivas stood up, surprising the one from Arkney on his left. Tristan was showing off his sword when the bow wielder next to him called for silence.

To turn the tide, Icthlarin and Amascut sought powerful allies to aid us. They found them far from here, in a place beyond this world. A powerful race of faceless ones. They became Icthlarin's Stern Judges.
Among the Stern Judges, there was a serpent. After my father [Osmumten] became Pharaoh, this serpent convinced the others to abandon us.
[Sliske]: The dwarves of Acheron uncovered it. They lost their home as a result. They fled south, but some remained under its control. They brought it with them.
Mysterious Voice 1: What am I looking at here? [Sliske]: An answer. Mysterious Voice 1: To what question? [Sliske]: What lies beyond?

Mysterious Voice 1: What became of these dwarves? [Sliske]: They succumbed. It had no further use for them. Mysterious Voice 1: Could it do the same to us? [Sliske]: I have shielded it. It will do you no harm.

Mysterious Voice 1: Then we'd better not waste time. There are resources that can be diverted, though there will be pushback. [Sliske]: It will be dealt with. My companion will remain to oversee your research. She will ensure that you face no barriers.

[Sliske]: Have the undercity sealed, then remove the protections on the totem. We require a more thorough test. [The Whisperer]: And the researchers? [Sliske]: Their work is complete. Do with them as you wish.

Mysterious Voice 2: The undercity is being sealed. They say the fortress has fallen. Mysterious Voice 3: Sealed? On whose orders? Mysterious Voice 2: Well... yours. Mysterious Voice 3: I gave no such order. Round up the centurions! We have a traitor among us. [The Whisperer]: No. Mysterious Voice 3: You! This was your doing! [The Whisperer]: You have served your Empire well, High Magister, but that servitude is at an end. Now it is time for a new one to begin.
I never saw [the priest] again. He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him... I heard little of what they said, but I did hear what she called him. Sliske.
He encouraged us to join him. We abandoned the cause of Saradomin and became followers of Guthix.
Our new leader taught us the ways of the druids, including an ancient ritual that had the power to awaken Guthix himself.
When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. The ritual also destroyed the protective enchantments on their prison.

quote:
* Sliske: You and I have been friends for some time now. Don't you remember?
* Wizard Persten: Don't you remember how we survived the horrors of the Scar?
* Assassin: Don't you remember how we escaped Ghorrock Prison?
* Ketla: Don't you remember how we held back the shadows of Lassar?
* Kasonde: Don't you remember how we overcame the infected Stranglewood?

quote: Over and over, we have our ritual. Over and over, we doom one of our kind to the endless void. [...] But the Horn will be our salvation. I will use it to break the cycle that has shackled us for so long. We will finally be free.

From what I can tell, he is completely mad. He roams the Wilderness, killing all who he comes across without mercy. Even his own kind do not escape his fury. He's known to battle the justiciar quite regularly, perhaps they are old enemies.
[Derwen] seems to take great interest in the other two creatures. Maybe he is trying to keep a balance between them.
[Who's this Justiciar of the Owl?] Saradomin's wisest of servants. It surprises me that you've not heard of his many feats.
These plants were grown personally by Zachariah, the Justiciar of the Owl. Anything he plants blossoms with unimaginable vigour. You may have noticed that he has a love for lilies.
...he has given us the task of protecting it [the Stone].
Zamorak has tasked his collector with finding the Eye. I will hunt him down before he does, along with any others who would try to claim it.
Strange, when I saw him last he had no magical hand to speak of...

quote: It was indeed me who sent that parcel. Had I revealed the contents of the journal myself, I would likely have just been dismissed as trying to create a rift between our two houses. Phileas was the perfect third party.
I imagine [Martin] also didn't mention that he used to work for the Council that he hates so much.
I'm sure Lydia didn't tell you everything about herself either. We were together once, you know. But she was ever loyal to the Council. In the end she decided I wasn't her type.
When I worked for the Council, I was young and naive. But over time, I came to see the truth.
I was helping to manage the treasury at the time. We had a big donation come in from a private businessman.
He wanted the money to go towards improved education in Port Piscarilius. He felt it would help with the crime levels there.
...they used only a small amount for that. They spent the rest on castle renovations.
They claimed the increase in castle tourism would make more money in the long run.
I walked out that same day. Soon after, I founded Kourend's Royal Society. We've been a bane for the Council ever since.
Would you believe it that apparently [Sophia Hughes] went and summoned a demon in Port Piscarilius? That made a lot of people angry.
Martin. He's leader of Kourend's Royal Society. He knows more about the last royal family than anyone. If anyone can help you find Rose, it's him.
Martin Holt, I am arresting you for inciting violence against the Kourend Council. [...] You have encouraged people to take up arms against the rightful rulers of Kourend.
They took [Martin] to the Shayzien Prison, just west of the city.
Can you believe it? The coronation of a king! Truth be told, there were times I wondered if this day would ever come.[...] And to think they even let us vote on [Rose's Accord] as well! Fantastic!
When the people voted on Rose's Accord, they voted for the Hosidius family to become the new royal family.
My job is to advise King Artur and ensure his actions have a positive impact on the people that he now rules.
Our purpose was to wait. But we saw the world burn. We could not stand by and watch. So we left our people. Left our home. And took on a new purpose.
Alas, according to records, the party never returned and were declared to have perished in the field.
Without the power of the Dark Altar, Xeric would have become mortal.

This [unstable] altar, it seems to give off the same power as the Dark Altar... I believe this altar was created to amplify the power of the Dark Altar, allowing it to reach areas it previously couldn't.
Sadly, the kingdom of Great Kourend is besieged by lizard creatures and it is not possible to get out of the kingdom just yet.
...we've pushed the lizardmen back to the point where we're finally able to allow citizens such as yourself into the region.
Not too long ago you couldn't safely travel around these parts. Too many lizardmen. But then some Hosidius explorers discovered how fertile this land was.
Lord Hosidius made a deal with Lord Shayzien and the lizardmen were cleared out to make room for the Farming Guild.
If [the lizardmen invade], we can quickly call in reinforcements if required.
Luckily the lizardmen have been focusing their efforts elsewhere. They haven't tried to come up here yet.
We set [a human bank] up here to help your kind serve the balance with us.
For example, here in Fortis, you'll find yourself surrounded by Perican archetecture, whereas over in the Tlati Rainforest, the influence of the Talkasti remains clear.

Imafore soon found himself facing as much resistance from within as he did from Kourend. The end result was predictable. Imafore and his forces found themselves trapped between two armies at the Battle of the Proudspire. He was captured and executed, bringing an end to the Tullus dynasty.

It was built by those who wandered these lands before we did. They worshipped Ralos and Ranul just as we now do. The obelisk was a site of great religious importance to them, and so it is to us as well.

[The purpose of the obelisk] is something we sadly don't know. It is why the obelisk is especially important to those who serve Ranul. It is a reminder of the importance in ensuring knowledge is preserved.
[The college is] found in the floating city of Tempestus!
You see, I found a poem in the College of Bards that told of the sanctuary below.
Apparently, this isn't the first time this illness has beset Slepe. In fact, they say it's how the town was named.
Glough sent me to Karamja to meet him. I delivered a large amount of gold.

Glough paid me to go to this gnome on a hill. I gave the gnome a seal and he gave me some Daconia rocks to give to Glough. I've been doing it for weeks, this time though Glough locked me up here! I just don't understand it.
It's sad but I think Glough was right. Humans are planning to invade and wipe out the tree gnomes!

My daughter betrayed me long ago. When I rejected Lowerniel Drakan's attempts to unite my clan with his, she chose to conspire with him. She made an attempt on my life, leaving me for dead, before claiming my clan and title as her own.

I'd give [Verzik] the credit over Ranis. The two of them shared a love for playing with their food rather than eating it. They hatched all kinds of schemes together. During the war, they managed to capture a justiciar, one of Efaritay's most elite warriors. They tortured him for days, until he gave them what they needed. [Player: Which was?] A secret tunnel, leading directly into Efaritay's castle. The tunnel was here, in this very graveyard. Once they were inside, capturing Ascertes was easy.
In some ways, I think Lowerniel was a bit disappointed the fighting was over. The pair were still greatly rewarded, however. Verzik ended up getting Efaritay's castle. It was quite the boon for her.

Besides, with all the work you put in, it would have felt wrong to just abandon her. [...] I've found her to be quite the inspiration. Thanks to her, I've decided to give the whole place a bit of a sprucing up. [Ranis Drakan: You're replacing all the challenges?] Absolutely! Those old ones were getting dull. It's time for some fresh excitement in this place.
You can thank Lowerniel for this one. He found these eggs in an arachnid nest north of Darkmeyer. He thought you might be able to use them in your nylocas breeding program.
Ranis Drakan: Bloat? Not the most elaborate of names, is it? Verzik Vitur: A crude name for a crude creation.

Ranis Drakan: A new nylocas? Verzik Vitur: The athanatos! Isn't it magnificent! Ranis Drakan: It's quite a sight to behold. Verzik Vitur: I have you and Lowerniel to thank for this one. This is the result of those eggs you gave me.

Verzik Vitur: The thing I need is something with the ability to regenerate. Nylocas are strong in numbers, but far too weak on their own. Ranis Drakan: Hmm... I think I know just the thing. When we created the Maiden, we experimented heavily in that area. Verzik Vitur: Ah, of course. You and your haemalchemy. Ranis Drakan: Well in the end it wasn't actually haemalchemy that gave us the answer. It came in the form of a gift from the old queen. Verzik Vitur: Not another of her plants was it? Ranis Drakan: Precisely that! Specifically the hespori. Their bark has wonderful regenerative abilities.

Verzik Vitur: Power over the Shadow Realm you say? That takes me back to the old empire. Ranis Drakan: That was the inspiration. Alas, the experiments didn't really go anywhere in the end. Verzik Vitur: Such a pity. Still, [Sotetseg] will make for a fine new challenge here.

Verzik Vitur: The last King of the yarasa... I never thought I'd see one of their kind again. Does this mean Lowerniel finally found a way home? Ranis Drakan: It would seem so, but he did not enlighten me on how he did it.

This is the one Ranis. This is my new Queen Nylocas. All that work has finally paid off. The queen nylocas bites Verzik and dies. Ouch! You little... Oh... [...] I really thought this was the one... Back to square one I guess. What a waste.

Verzik Vitur: I feel... I feel... wrong. Vulcan Orvoros: My lady, as I've already said, we really should take you to my surgery in Darkmeyer. Whatever that nylocas did, it was no normal bite. Verzik Vitur: No! This is my home! You will not take me! [...] Doctor... It's... inside me! Vulcan Orvoros: My lady? Verzik Vitur: I can feel it! Help me! Verzik explodes.
Destroy the witness... Let us dine on his corpse! [...] The rule of the vampyres is over... The rule of the nylocas has begun...
Now that was quite the show! I haven't been that entertained in a long time. Of course, you know I can't let you leave here alive. Time for your final performance...
Back again for more? I admire your perseverance. Shall we begin?
When we created the Maiden, we experimented heavily in that area.
Precisely that! Specifically the hespori. Their bark has wonderful regenerative abilities.
I must say, I find the name you've given her to be quite interesting. Not the kind of thing I'd have expected from you.
It seemed an ironically fitting role for her, given that fun little narrative you came up with. Besides, with all the work you put in, it would have felt wrong to just abandon her.
The Maiden of Sugadinti. Such an ironic name.
My husband went there, trying to win freedom from the blood-gatherers by surviving her arena, but he never returned. No-one does.
I tried for years to escape, with my son, Suro, to make a better life for ourselves in Misthalin. I scraped together enough money to bribe a boatman to get us out.
The journey was tough. Some men in pink hoods attacked our boat, shouting at us to go back where we belonged, and to keep out of their country. In the struggle, the boat overturned.

It was dark, and I couldn't find Suro in the water. I swam as deep as I could, until my lungs screamed, but I couldn't find him. He wasn't good at swimming. Eventually I got myself to the shore. The sun was rising, and I found Suro there. On the shore, where the water had dumped his... body.
I've done alright in Misthalin, I guess. I know a bit of magic, and the local gentry pay me well for my scrying skills. I'm good at turning a profit on Grand Exchange trades too.

I managed to find the remnants of the ancient civilisation that the stories talked about. It seems people used to worship a god there years ago in numbers far greater than a simple cult following. Sadly there is little remaining so I have nothing else to tell. As soon as I entered this area the ground swallowed me whole. I felt there was something watching, waiting. It's like there is some evil power under the ground that wanted me to suffer. As if it got some sort of empowerment from it. At least what ever it is, it doesn't want to reveal itself to the world yet...
[The book of Haricanto] was stolen when our port was raided by pirates many years ago, and never seen since.
For the rest of us to live, one of us must die. Many will go to great lengths to ensure they are not the one who is sacrificed.
notes: Said while disguised as Big Fish.

quote: Aargh... Muspah! Wait... What...? Hmm... just another nightmare.
Are you not wondering how I ended up in that cell? [...] It was that Mahjarrat. Seems he doesn't think much of you either, as he was also responsible for your own imprisonment.
