quote: [Black Knight Captain: No need to... get upset... you're scaring the cat.] 'The CAT'? She's not 'THE CAT'! She's Maemi... aren't you dear....
I'll be waiting for you in the north, Akthanakos.
I'll see you in the North.
The fortress to the east is all that remains on the surface, but there is much still hidden below.

You see, we have not always lived in Weiss. We used to live further south, near the dwarf town they call Keldagrim, until we were driven out... That Wise Young Man drove us out into the barren icy mountains.

Alas, that was a long time ago. I've since passed away. (...) Oh we all are here! Santa gave us the opportunity to stay here in this sanctuary. (...) That's just the thing, while we are in here we can keep our mortal body with Santa's magic.
After the Shayzien Army cleared out the lizardmen in this area, I founded this guild with some fellow Hosidius farmers.
The heat of the volcano allows us to grow things here that would never survive in the climate of Kourend. The discoveries we have made here are worth the extra risk.
[Player: What's a Hespori?] A rare carnivorous plant originally from Morytania. When grown, the plant becomes conscious and highly aggressive. They are truly fascinating.
They were grown here back when this place was still known as Hallowvale. The Saradominist Queen of the region used them as weapons against the vampyres.

When we created the Maiden, we experimented heavily in [regeneration]. [...] Well in the end it wasn't actually haemalchemy that gave us the answer. It came in the form of a gift from the old queen. [...] Specifically the hespori. Their bark has wonderful regenerative abilities.
If you want to go further afield, why not have a look at the ominous Pillars of Zanash, the mysterious marble pillars located just West of the city?
That particular shrine has existed since before Witchaven was even founded. (...) Over one hundred and fifty years old in fact.
The shrine was abandoned when the village came into being. Since then it has fallen into disrepair and the other less savoury elements have moved in.
The history of that shrine should not be overlooked. It is ancient beyond your knowledge and much that shaped our history is contained within its walls.
The Kourend Royal Guard protect and serve the ruler of Kourend. As their leader, I am responsible for ensuring that the Royal Guard are well trained and well supplied.
Back when I was a girl, there was this Shayzien patrol that would go past our house each morning. Every day I would run out to wave at them as they went by.

For as long as I can remember, I always wanted to join the army. 'Become a farmer or a chef,' my parents would say to me. 'The army isn't for you.' But I knew what I wanted, and I knew nothing would stop me from getting it.

I remember a gang of thieves a few years back that used them heavily. The kids could get places the adults couldn't. No one ever suspected them either. They were such a problem that the Council had to get Lord Shayzien to send some soldiers in to deal with them. Lydia was one of them.
The Council had them all thrown in prison, even the children. Lydia was distraught.
I'm sure Lydia didn't tell you everything about herself either. We were together once, you know.
...she was ever loyal to the Council. In the end she decided I wasn't her type, and went off with that Captain Ginea instead. Of course, that didn't work out either.
Ah, so you're the adventurer who's been cooking up a storm around here. Well you'll be pleased to know your hard work was all for nothing. Councillor Hughes has escaped. Lucky her.

Alright, you can help. But for the duration of this investigation, you're working for me. What I say goes, [...] Right now we don't have any leads on where Councillor Hughes might have gone. I'm heading over to her home to see if there's anything there that can help us.
You have betrayed the trust of Yama, Sophia Hughes. You have used his generosity to your own advantage. For this, your life is forfeit.
Councillor Andrews may have been all nice to you, but he's furious with me. He's blamed me for what happened in Port Piscarilius.
You'd think they'd have some loyalty after all we did! After what we did to him. After what we did to his girl! We were in it together until it no longer suited them!
Martin. He's leader of Kourend's Royal Society. He knows more about the last royal family than anyone. If anyone can help you find Rose, it's him.

There was an Arceuus mage. He was an expert in curses, and he realised what was happening. He gave us the poison for the King. [...] By then, it was already too late. The King had deteriorated too much. There was only one solution.

The poison they gave her irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure. Someone else could make the potions, but all they do is prolong her suffering. This is no life for anyone. The truth is, Rose died long ago. All that's left now is an empty shell.
We, the leaders of the five houses of Great Kourend, declare that the Kourend Council is no longer fit to rule. As such, you are relieved of your positions with immediate effect.

I'm sure Lydia didn't tell you everything about herself either. We were together once, you know. But she was ever loyal to the Council. In the end she decided I wasn't her type, and went off with that Captain Ginea instead. Of course, that didn't work out either. One day she'll stop blaming her problems on everyone else.
Unlike the Shayzien Army, the Royal Guard serve the ruler of the kingdom directly.
The Kourend Royal Guard protect and serve the ruler of Kourend. As their leader, I am responsible for ensuring that the Royal Guard are well trained and well supplied.
The Royal Guard was established by King Byrne I. He felt that it was dangerous for Shayzien House to control the only military in the kingdom, so he decided to establish a small one of his own.
[King Kharedst] married late and his wife... Unfortunately didn't survive bringing Rose into this world.
Apparently Rose and her father would often make riddles for each other. I'm guessing she was quite fond of them.
Are you saying the man I sold those trinkets to was the king?! Those were dark objects, corrupted with powerful magic. Dark magic.
The flask was cursed. Some dark magic. He stopped being himself. Started saying things. Things he would do to people. To the citizens!
There was an Arceuus mage. He was an expert in curses, and he realised what was happening. He gave us the poison for the King.
By then, it was already too late. The King had deteriorated too much. There was only one solution.
Kourend's last King, Kharedst IV, had only one child when he died. She was too young to take the throne, so the Kourend Council was formed to look after things until she came of age.
We didn't want to kill her. She didn't deserve that. The mage gave us a potion. He said it would stop her revealing the truth.
I did some research while you were gone. [Councillor Orson] wasn't lying. The poison they gave [Rose] irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure.
Alas, she was very close to her father and his sudden death drove her to insanity.
After what happened, public life was no place for her. The Council arranged for her to move away so she could escape all of that.
With no suitable ruler, the Kourend Council was made permanent.
I'm fairly certain it was destroyed... At least, I recall seeing a man removing the pages...

The poison they gave her irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure. Someone else could make the potions, but all they do is prolong her suffering. This is no life for anyone. The truth is, Rose died long ago. All that's left now is an empty shell.
In honour of her sacrifice, I name this declaration Rose's Accord. With it, the Kingdom of Great Kourend will no longer be a kingdom divided.
When the people voted on Rose's Accord, they voted for the Hosidius family to become the new royal family.

He's a demon of some sorts, but he doesn't seem to have any actual presence in Kourend yet. In fact, until recently, he had no connection to the cult. It does sound odd, but back then they were known as the Disciples of Chaos. They were just a small Zamorakian cult of little note.
My master wishes you not to kill his minions without an agenda. You may only slay within the Chasm that which you have been assigned by a Slayer Master.
You modified my memory?! That's only the second time someone has done that to me, and I wasn't very happy about it then either!
It's not a distinction the Fremennik particularly care for. To us, he has always been a hero to be respected, not a god to be worshipped. They say he felt the same way.

Our ancient leader, who first discovered the rune essence mine here on Lunar Isle, travelled far and wide searching for more places of power. He and his followers built altars all over Gielinor - which you use today to create runes - and at their height they made runes by the crateful.
name: moonclan

quote: We specialise in 'acquiring' valuable antiquities from around the city and shipping them to our friends overseas.
You're right with that one [laddie/lass]. Someone or something has made a small hole in the Doors.
It's not much, but it's enough for that Wintertodt to be able to draw some power into the prison. Probably why them fiery lot have had so much trouble recently.

[Player: Does this mean the Wintertodt won't be a threat anymore?] That should be the case in the long run. I suspect it will take a long time though. The Doors were damaged for a while and the Wintertodt will have gained a lot of power. I reckon that magic lot will have to do their fiery tricks for a bit longer before everything is back to normal.
He's been with our family for twenty years... that's 140 in dog years!
I am from a place far in the Kharidian Desert. So far that you would not have heard of it, so there is no point in me telling you the name of this place.
The reason why you never see me around here often is because I only ever make the trip to Al Kharid around Easter time. This is around the time my wares ripen and sell for their highest price.
They [the dragonkin] were bound to it long ago. To use the Stone causes them unimaginable pain, and grants them immense power.
name: dragonkin-1

quote: Only a few gave in to the anger of the curse.
The Eye of Saradomin is one name for this artefact, though it has had many others. For example, we in Crux Eqal know it as the Fist of Guthix.
It's been known by many names, and most of them have been long forgotten. The Eye of Saradomin was one. The Fist of Guthix was another.
loc: Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire

quote: Apparently, the one known as Primus was being defended by Saradominists. Perseriya and her fleet were trying to claim it, but things clearly didn't go as planned, hence them ending up here.[...]Isn't it obvious? It must be the Eye.
V was different. Stories tell of how he unlocked the potential of magic with the single touch of a stone.
The Fremennik were actually the first to discover how to make runes.

The stone was clearly not of this world, and the mere touch of it unlocked something within the mind of V---. As we know, the stone was instantly removed by those powers who walk a higher Astral Path than ourselves, but its very existence showed V--- possibilities that had never occurred to our kind before.
name: path

quote: It was then [after the Betrayal of Zaros] that the other gods appeared and banished Zamorak from the world completely for daring to kill one of their kind, although as it turned out it didn't quite work out that way for them, when he returned stronger than ever, a god himself.
... [Saradomin] has given us the task of protecting [the Eye].
You must build a sanctuary for the Eye. The forces of chaos already seek to reobtain it, as do countless others.
Zamorak has tasked his collector with finding the Eye. I will hunt him down before he does, along with any others who would try to claim it.
This temple was built to house a powerful artefact. Many sought to claim this artefact for themselves, including servants of the Fallen Empire.
In their attempt to claim the artefact, they used magic they did not understand. The rift to the Scar was created as a result.
The Eye was removed after the battle, but not before the Justiciar of the Lion used it to seal the rift once more.
She then created us, the Guardians of the Rift, to protect this place in the event the rift was ever reopened.
They say that an object of great power was once stored in this very cave. Apparently, the presence of this object created the daeyalt deposits.
The God Wars are over... as long as the thing they were fighting over remains hidden.

The stone was clearly not of this world, and the mere touch of it unlocked something within the mind of V---. As we know, the stone was instantly removed by those powers who walk a higher Astral Path than ourselves, but its very existence showed V--- possibilities that had never occurred to our kind before.
name: path

quote: They [the dragonkin] were bound to it long ago. To use the Stone causes them unimaginable pain, and grants them immense power.
name: dragonkin-1

quote: Not all of us. Only a few gave in to the anger of the curse. Only a few waged war on you. But you were not willing to distinguish. And now, neither am I.
This here is the Gauntlet, the finest creation of the Amlodd clan. It was built years ago to help train Prifddinas' finest warriors and survivalists.

Once I was a merchant. I worked hard and became wealthy, very wealthy. I was brave too, storing my possessions in two great chests here, where few would dare to interfere with them. But I was not strong enough. One day a witch allied with the pirates of the north; between their strength and her magic, they killed me. The pirates carried one of my chests away to their ship.
I do not know why Krystilia sends adventurers to find my keys instead of looting the chest herself. Perhaps it amuses her to send people into this land to risk their lives.
Sarachnis can be found in the Forthos Dungeon. She is the mother of the temple spiders, be careful not to get overwhelmed.
I know of Gorlah. It's an old shrine north of Prifddinas, a place for quiet worship away from the city.
Eh, some poor sap walks in carrying one, gets himself killed, and the creature just hangs on to it as a trophy? I can see it.
It is a hard place to describe. We often refer to it as another plane, but that isn't quite accurate. If anything, it is more like a plane that sits between all other planes.
It [the Abyss] can be used as an effective hub for teleportation. In fact, all teleportation that we know of uses the Abyss, you just don't realise it.
Whenever you use a teleport spell, that spell is actually travelling through the Abyss and using it to link two places together.

You see, time and space work differently in the Abyss. For example, you can travel to the Abyss, walk a few steps and then exit, only to find yourself somewhere completely different from where you entered. You might even find yourself on a different plane. You can also enter the Abyss and spend days there, but on your return, only moments have passed.
We broke through to the Abyss, seeking allies for our cause, but instead I ended up a prisoner in this place, unable to leave, while the God Wars continued without me.
Bringing me those body parts from the Sires has now granted me enough teleportation energy to leave this living hell hole.

By remaining here and holding this rift open, I am providing a permanent link between normal space and this strange dimension. As long as my spell remains in effect, we have the capability to teleport into the Abyss.

Before she claimed them, my parents would sometimes tell me a story of her origin. They told me of a group of shamans who performed an unknown ritual in the hope of gaining great power. The ritual went wrong, though, and instead, they unleashed the Nightmare on this world.
For generations, she terrorised the island of Ashihama, my home. I lost a lot of good friends to her. Sometimes, I even thought I would lose myself. For some, the nightmares become too much to bear.
I found the totems deep within the caves. Someone far smarter than you or I had worked out how to make them. But they perished before they could use them against her.
Thanks to the Nightmare, the caves beneath our home are mostly unexplored. There's all sorts of things down there, provided you're brave enough to enter.
Everything has a weakness, including the Nightmare, and eventually we found it. We drove her off the island, but she managed to endure.
We took up arms against the Nightmare because we had to, not because we wanted to. We are a peaceful race, and most were all too eager to lay down their weapons once the Nightmare was gone.

My kind believe in something called Mo Kal. It means that anything bad that could happen, will happen. The others may have forgotten this, but I have not. The Nightmare may have left my home, but I won't rest until I know for sure that she can never return.

The people here are ill, suffering from a deep sleep from which few wake. They call it the Sleeper Plague. The illness made these people easy prey for the Nightmare, so she made this place her new home.
Thanks to the Sleeper Plague, her power has grown faster than it ever did on Ashihama. If she is allowed to grow too strong, there won't be any way to stop her.

I've managed to contain her within this section of the dungeon. She has no desire to leave for the moment. She has no need to, after all. But make no mistake, I won't be able to stop her if she decides to move on.
The creature down there, the one that Siren calls the Nightmare. It has been invading Mother's mind, feeding on her.
The horror that has manifested itself in Mother's mind is far stronger than the one fought in the Nightmare's dream.
Finally, I've been cutting down the same tree over and over again. I have level 15 Woodcutting now. I'm going insane.

[Player: I'm looking for Traitorous Ali.] He was just here! Look, he's even left his drink on the table by those barrels. Must have nipped out to go to the toilet. He might be gone a while though. The nearest outhouse is all the way over on Fossil Island.
We trolls are named after the first thing we try to eat, an' some things are kinda inevitable in a big snowy land with almost no toilets.
[Player: Why are you waiting by this hole?] Ever seen a toilet around here?

[Nirrie: We are a gestalt entity. We each have our own body, but our minds] [Tirrie: are united and we all think as one. Well except when Hallak doth leaveth] [Nirrie: the toilet seat up.] That's the way it's meant to be!
Can you find my teacher? I need the toilet!

Hey, serf, what business have you in there? [Player: I'm looking for the toilet.] That is a worthy pursuit. Many people spend the holidays wistfully dreaming of a better world, turning to empty fantasies and false cheers to conceal their disappointment at reality. But you, by focusing on such a practical pursuit, may truly bring about a better world while the dreamers achieve nothing. I salute you, and wish you success in your quest!
Oh, we spiders understand humans very well. We've been around you for years. (...) Usually in a cupboard or attic, or toilet, where we won't disturb anyone much.
I bet ye've never had to beat a dozen zombies to death with a blunt toothpick! [Player: That's right. Have you?] No, I've spent most of my time in the toilet to be honest.
Well, I'm not a priest, but I must admit I've been praying fervently since the zombies arrived. [Player: For anything in particular?] A new pair of trousers. Those things are scary.
We dug smelly hole in prison so Mother's prisoners wouldn't go all over floor, but it not very convenient.
[Player: Great, will I be able to take a nap in it?] Don't be silly; everyone knows that true warriors don't ever sleep...or perform many other bodily functions, for that matter.
My Arm not like to say so earlier, but you bin smellin' like you done a whoopsie.
I've seen that one before. It's yours now.

Queen Efaritay was a renowned botanist. She used this to her advantage many times during the war, breeding all kinds of plant life to use against us. One of these plants was the Blisterwood tree. The icyene used the sap of this tree to create poisons that were deadly to vampyres.
But from what I can tell, even when chopped away, the wood of the tree is very much alive. It shifts and grows in unpredictable ways, rendering our immunities useless.
[Player: Those nets are strange.] Ah, made from the finest thread in all the land. [Player: And that is?] Gnome hair.

This place was built long before the city of Darkmeyer existed, back when this land was known as Hallowvale. The Sepulchre was used as a resting place for Hallowvale's loyal followers of Saradomin. [...] The dead here were buried with the wealth they had in life. To protect these riches, the Saradominists enchanted the statues within the Sepulchre to create various defences.

One day the justiciar sent word to me that I should begin work on securing the Sepulchre. He feared an invasion from the followers of the Dark Lord. [...] The justiciar said he was going to confront these forces but that I should stay to protect the secrets within this place.

Day by day we worked our way down to the final floor. As we progressed further, we became more experienced at creating the traps. Each one was more deadly than the last. Eventually, when our work was done, I performed the last rites for each of my followers and sealed them within the coffins on the final floor. Finally, I did the same for myself. The knowledge of how to disarm the traps died with us.

[Player: Okay... So I presume you want me to get some of this treasure for you? Does Efaritay know about this? It doesn't seem like the kind of thing she would appreciate.] It was actually on her orders that we first started doing it. She was very keen for us to gather as much of the old currency of this land as possible.

Not just any silvthrill. Pure silvthrill. The smiths of Hallowvale were able to perfect the process of creating the alloy, making it far more powerful than the crude form used in your flail. Unfortunately, the secrets to that process have long been lost, but pure silvthrill can still be found, provided you know where to look. (Efaritay shows you some hallowed marks.) Hallowed marks. The old currency of Hallowvale. When Sugadinti and I first managed to send one of his disciples to my former home, I made sure that gathering these was their first priority. Doing so required them to desecrate the tombs of my people. To have to resort to such methods...

Yes... There was some debate over if we should end our work here. It is true that the icyene in particular was keen to see it come to an end. However, the tombs have already been desecrated. That cannot be undone now, and while Drakan may be gone, it is wise that we be adequately prepared for any possibility.
Many sought to claim this artefact for themselves, including servants of the Fallen Empire.
The armies of the Ruinous Powers were far stronger than our own. That was until Icthlarin's Stern Judges joined the fray.
My ancestors lived far to the North of here, and our lands stretched from the sea in the East to the river Lum, and the mountain of ice. From coast to coast, North to South, our domain was absolute.

…the enemies that sought to destroy us through their petty jealousies. (…) The spiteful Saradomin and pathetic Zamorak warred with each other, but the hatred they had for each other was as nothing to the hatred they held towards us!
Oh yes, the dragon riders, Mahjarrat, demons and vampyre warriors made up the bulk of the force, but I wager I was their equal in all ways of combat.
name: Bulk

quote: It started during the rule of my grandmother. An ever-expanding empire to the north set their sights on our lands. War soon broke out.
…and if truth be told, there was a fair amount of dissent amongst... 'his' followers anyway.

The Empty Lord chose to ally himself with the dark creatures of this world, fully aware that their own natures would cause them to rally against his rule and, take every opportunity they could to betray him.
Let us just say that he was a fearsome deity, whose strength was greater than all the gods we knew of on this realm at the time.
…there was a growing faction amongst them who were plotting to overthrow their master.
…it had come to my attention that the Mahjarrat who had been liberated from the control of Icthlarin did not much appreciate one form of slavery to another…

Lord Zamorak and his most trusted compatriots, namely myself, Hazeel, Drakan, Thammaron and Zemouregal made plans to overthrow our lord using the god-weapon, and by pledging allegiance to Zamorak as our master…
…were each to be given a large piece of land as our own in return.
Myself and the rest of Zamoraks honour guard were formulating stratagems in our battle-tent, when that sneaky messenger Kharrim came in offering to sell us the god-staff of Armadyl!
…the Empty Lord, who seemed to lose his footing slightly, and fell in such a way so that the staff plunged deeper into his body, but also impaled Lord Zamorak with it at the same time...
When my Lord Zamorak first got his taste of godhood!
…and as the Empty Lord faded from this world completely…

It was then that the other gods appeared and banished Zamorak from the world completely for daring to kill one of their kind, although as it turned out it didn't quite work out that way for them, when he returned stronger than ever, a god himself. But the god wars were another story entirely...
With him gone, the empire collapsed. War broke out soon after.
Although their god was gone, many Zarosians fought to keep his empire alive.
But we did not succumb without fighting!
Among them was Nex. She was Zaros' most powerful weapon, and she led a great army to try and restore his empire.
name: Nex

quote: The forces of Saradomin knew that Nex needed to be dealt with. They were able to lure her into these caverns. After great effort and sacrifice, they managed to place Nex and her followers into a frozen, enchanted sleep.
When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. (…) He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him. (…) Sliske.
name: Sliske

quote: After our great mistake, four opposing armies united to contain the evil again. They managed to reseal the prison…
With each battle they waged, we lost more and more land, unable to fight on all fronts, and were pushed further and further South into this gods-forsaken desert.
Our greatest hero, Azzanadra, was finally trapped in a strange stone structure to the South of here, and bound within by terrible powers...
And with that our lands, our homes, our very lives were stolen from us!
Nex posed such a danger, that the four armies temorarily joined forces to drive her back into the prison. They resealed it, but were unable to fix the enchantments we destroyed.
No. Among the Stern Judges, there was a serpent. After my father became Pharaoh, this serpent convinced the others to abandon us. [They joined the enemy?] They did.
name: Serpent

quote: There was once a time where humans and vampyres lived together in a great empire.
name: Vanescula

quote: During the great war, our forces were decimated by the servants of the Ruinous Powers.
If the shining cities no longer stand, then it means that we must have failed my lord...
Melting rune and adamant would normally result in a simple blend. [...] But with the right amount of heat, pressure and air... There. Chromium. Alloyed rune and adamant.

Chromium is one of our most significant discoveries. [...] Chromium lies at the heart of Lassar. It is in our golems, our lights, even our walls. We have invested a lot to make producing it 'easy'. It was not always this way...
Before the God Wars, a settlement of the old empire was found here.
name: Old

quote: The fortress to the east is all that remains on the surface, but there is much still hidden below.
A great prison...
Do the shining spires of Lassar still stand?

Not just any silvthrill. Pure silvthrill. The smiths of Hallowvale were able to perfect the process of creating the alloy, making it far more powerful than the crude form used in your flail. Unfortunately, the secrets to that process have long been lost, but pure silvthrill can still be found, provided you know where to look. (Efaritay shows you some hallowed marks.)
They say that an object of great power was once stored in this very cave. Apparently, the presence of this object created the daeyalt deposits.

With us having outlawed the practice of vampyrification, we have started using the labs to explore the creation of artificial blood instead. Curiously, we've already had some luck with daeyalt of all things. It seems that the very substance that is the key to making vampyres can also potentially contribute to feeding them. While it makes sense in many ways, it was also rather... unexpected.
But from what I can tell, even when chopped away, the wood of the tree is very much alive. It shifts and grows in unpredictable ways, rendering our immunities useless.
One of these plants was the Blisterwood tree. The icyene used the sap of this tree to create poisons that were deadly to vampyres.

Queen Efaritay was a renowned botanist. She used this to her advantage many times during the war, breeding all kinds of plant life to use against us. One of these plants was the Blisterwood tree. The icyene used the sap of this tree to create poisons that were deadly to vampyres. However, I've always suspected the tree might have other uses. Clearly the researchers in the Haemalchemy Laboratory thought the same. [...] It seems that the bark of the Blisterwood tree can be used to create weapons that are deadly to my kind.

They are a symbol of the wise. You see, owls can see the light in the darkest of places. [...] These creatures have the blessing of Saradomin and the wisdom of ages long past. They are the watchers of the Hallowed Sepulchre. The last defence against unseen evils.
The greatest White Knights are buried here, after a lifetime in the service of Saradomin.
I'd heard rumours that there was an Abbey up here somewhere, which sounded marvellous, but I seem to be in the wrong place.
Callisto killed my father. After hearing of a great beast in the heart of the Wilderness, he took it upon himself to bring him down.
As a token of my own thanks, I give you access to the pass through Arandar. You'll find the start of the trail in the far north east of the woods.
Those that you know as mourners are in fact elves in service to Lord Iorwerth. We regularly see them crossing the Arandar mountain pass and into the east.

Many years back, before even I was around, there were two rival family farms not far from where we're standing. Every year the village would hold a 'Finest Swine in Show' prize at the annual faire. The same farmer would win year after year without fail. Driven mad with jealousy, his rival decided to hire a dodgy dark wizard to give him an edge over the competition. The wizard attempted to alter the pig's appearance. I'm sure you can guess how well that went!
Long story short, the mutant, what we now know as a Sourhog, went on a brief rampage and escaped. It must have somehow managed to reproduce, because people have reported seeing them in groups.
Rumors are, they live in deep underground caverns, scavenging what they can find.

Yes, it is a common name. I also know of Party Pete, Parroty Pete, Postie Pete, Pirate Pete, Petrified Pete and 'Picarron' Pete. The Makeover Mage has used the name Pete too. Although we are not related, the shared bond of that name can be a comfort in dark times.
We [Armadyleans] were here to claim something. To protect it. But everything else is unclear.
Big High War God use the shiny to kill the chickens! Now we clear up the rest!
Sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but I think this 'shiny' might have killed you as well.
Until that Nomad chap opened things up, this island was abandoned.

Yes, it is a common name. I also know of Party Pete, Parroty Pete, Postie Pete, Pirate Pete, Petrified Pete and 'Picarron' Pete. The Makeover Mage has used the name Pete too. Although we are not related, the shared bond of that name can be a comfort in dark times.
You may want to check out the orchard just north of the city. I hear no one has tended it since the blight infected the trees there. I imagine it will have plenty of rotten apples.

There are a load of islands out this way, and a lot of them have little bits and pieces like this scattered around. The way I see it, there must have been some people out here at one point, then they went away.
Trolls of Weiss, I am Snowflake, daughter of Mother, my father. Mother is dead, and I claim the throne.

The Chancellor called a meeting for all us local seafarin' folk and we agreed action must be taken! Ain't nothin' goin' t' take the seas from me, even if it is a powerful spirit! Anyway, it was decided that we'd setup a base 'ere amongst these ruins, and so the Spirit Anglers was formed! [...] Since moving in, we've been recruiting fisherfolk from all over, and some of the readin' types 'ave been studyin' Tempoross durin' our trips to subdue it.

It was dark, and I couldn't find Suro in the water. I swam as deep as I could, until my lungs screamed, but I couldn't find him. He wasn't good at swimming. Eventually I got myself to the shore. The sun was rising, and I found Suro there. On the shore, where the water had dumped his... body.
We [Armadyleans] were here to claim something. To protect it. But everything else is unclear.
Big High War God use the shiny to kill the chickens! Now we clear up the rest!
Sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but I think this 'shiny' might have killed you as well.
I'm Vicks, squire to Sir Culler Flife. He's away on a surveillance mission to Burthorpe, so he sent me down here to do some cleaning.
Well, I should thank you for finding my kitten that time. I have a terrible time keeping track of them, and I never know how many Gertrude has managed to sell.
The Forge powers the entire city, or what's left of it at least.
We've lost all contact with the capital. Worse, another dwarven clan has joined the Saradominists. They march upon the fortress as we speak.
Rumour has it [the Imcando] once lived in a great city in the far north. The city fell and now they are homeless.
It seems [the Imcando] have been promised a new home here in return for wiping us out.
Their leader is named Yonrith Lovakengj. He has fled to the west with his closest allies, but much of his army still remains.
Our methods would often differ from other dwarves. Whereas they just used traditional smithing techniques, we would combine them with magic as well.
We used our advanced Smithing knowledge to improve their form. Eventually, we were able to get them working again. We kept pushing with the golems. Many of them we imbued with magical energies.
Camdozaal was built upon the ruins of an older civilization. Little trace of them remained by the time we arrived. However, when building the city, ancient golems were discovered.

We learned of a horde of barbarians pillaging across the land, hunting down and killing anyone who dared use magic. We underestimated them. We believed our weapons would be enough to keep us safe. We were wrong. The barbarians brought ruin upon Camdozaal.
Most of my kind died as the city collapsed around them. Only a few of us survived until the end. Now, only I remain.
He's managed to keep the city going all these years, even with his lack of vision.
My lack of vision means I can't work an anvil like I used to.
Useless! Perhaps the headsman needs to take your head as well.
The city [Imcandoria] fell and now they are homeless.
It seems [the Imcando] have been promised a new home here in return for wiping us out.
Useless! Perhaps the headsman needs to take your head as well.
Their leader is named Yonrith Lovakengj. He has fled to the west with his closest allies, but much of his army still remains. Carnifex Maximus Vardorvis is in pursuit of him.
The Forge powers the entire city, or what's left of it at least.
[The Sacred Forge is] far older than I am. It was supposedly built in the earliest days of the city.
What I do know is that it's been imbued with powerful magic - some said that of the gods themselves.

I followed one called Lazim. He let slip that he had discovered the buried temple. Now the two others who were there are on the move. The General may find there are new players at the ritual this time.
Tell them: The planets are nearing alignment; we will meet in the place of half light and ice soon. Beware of the others, for though they are weak and few, they are cunning.
Yeah, it were made of stone, and it were odd. Some weird bone-head human saw me trying to nibble it, an' he got really upset an' chased me away. He kinda scary.
Anyway, my parents, they named me Odd Stone after that, and now we trolls not go anywhere near the place. Bone-head human was, like, really scary! And probably magic.
No, we trolls blocked all routes to snowfields from here. Don't want scary bone-head human coming to Weiss.

The ritual is used by our kind to ensure our survival, and the next one is fast approaching. [...] For the rest of us to live, one of us must die. Many will go to great lengths to ensure they are not the one who is sacrificed.
As fate would have it, we stand in a place where our senses mean nothing.
While the gods are useful for tedious matters such as granting prayers during combat, we of Arceuus have long moved beyond the need to pay them homage.
Saradomin is popular with many uneducated citizens of Kourend, but you may use our church to worship any god you prefer. That would be an ecumenical matter.
It appears to be manmade. I believe this altar was created to amplify the power of the Dark Altar, allowing it to reach areas it previously couldn't.
She was never afraid to get her own hands dirty. Did you know that before she was even my age, she became a champion in the Colosseum?

We are incredibly close, for we are united in Ralos' light, and in the love we share for Itzla. However, it would be fair to say that our relationship is not a conventional one, especially to an outsider. [Player: So how did it come about?] In times of old, the ruler of Varlamore would often unite with a Teokan of Ralos. His light guides us in all things, and a King or Queen will need that guidance more than most. Before she took the throne, the Queen made the decision to revive that old tradition. I was more than happy to accept.

I don't believe you've properly met my father. This is Servius, the Teokan of Ralos and the man whose life you saved. [Player: Your father? I didn't realise you were related.] Yes, very fun stuff. All a bit of a convoluted mess as well!
Most of our patrons are soldiers returning on leave from the frontlines.
We've just finished our first duties in the Lizardman Canyon. A few drinks at the Cloak and Stagger to celebrate is always traditional
This is the Shayzien Administration. The city of Shayzien is run from here.
A lot of focus right now is on the war with the lizardmen. Most senior members of the Shayzien Army, including Lord Shayzien himself, are working out of the Shayzien Encampment instead.
[Player: What's the gold chest for?] Any items that are in the chest will be dropped inside the balloons when you pull the lever!
The creature before you has advantages over a vyre. It is the perfect hunter. Once it gets a taste of its foes blood, it can track them anywhere.
I am whatever is needed of me.
I am a form undefined by natural laws, manifested by someone we mustn't speak of.
These objects of power are now gone, I have broken them into Fragments and spread across this iteration of the world.
Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.
I've limited and reset some of your memories, meaning you won't be able to interact with certain elements of this world.
Combat Masteries are powerful boons granted by me that enhance your combat abilities for the entire League.
This time, I have awakened the wrathful spirits of enemies across Gielinor.
Reality as you know it has many layers, all slightly different with their own rules. Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.

To give everything away at this point would be unwise, considering we are being watched even now. You should only be concerned about one thing. Being entertaining. That's the only way you will get out of this event alive...
Let's see if I can shuffle the pieces, create something new! The eyes beyond our own need new stories!

It's incredibly dangerous down there. We've lost far too many townsfolk already who underestimated the dangers. There are some fearsome traps and vicious monsters lurking in the darkness. [...] We've posted a number of guards there to hold back the scarab monsters. There is a barricaded trapdoor there that is a little complicated to open.

Glough left a code on the facility, which periodically needs to be entered if we wish to maintain the supply of power. Without going through the process of reinitialisation, we cannot power the mechanism which deploys the military gliders.
Later in the war, a great battle broke out in the Temple of Lost Ancients. I was a Saradominist soldier at the time, and I was among those who fought for him in that battle.
...many of us had grown tired of war. One of our priests discovered this. He came to us and revealed that he felt the same way, and that he had secretly converted to Guthix.
He encouraged us to join him. We abandoned the cause of Saradomin and became followers of Guthix.
Our new leader taught us the ways of the druids, including an ancient ritual that had the power to awaken Guthix himself. We believed this ritual to be the only way to end the war.
When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. The ritual also destroyed the protective enchantments on their prison.
I never saw him [the priest] again. He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him... I heard little of what they said, but I did hear what she called him. Sliske.
Nex posed such a danger, that the four armies temorarily joined forces to drive her back into the prison. They resealed it, but were unable to fix the enchantments we destroyed.
I was one of the first to fall after Nex was freed, but I didn't truly die. Something about our ritual tied me to this place. I've been trapped here ever since. Not dead, but not really alive either.
I fear you have been misled. There is no treasure here, only our great mistake.
If it helps, while my magic is limited here, I should still be able to transfer items in and out of the prison for you. Let me know if you'd like me to do this before you enter.

They wanted to see how far you'd go!
Nagua are creatures well versed in magic. Their reckless fighting style leaves them open to melee attacks.
For centuries, the magic used to seal the Moons has been woven into Neypotzli and the creatures that inhabit it. Naguanil is the magic of nature.
Mokhaiotl? The Tlati archive? That place is not for your kind. You misused the gifts you were granted. You are unworthy.
You should be careful of trusting the words of a nagua.
Nagua are not known for being reliable.
The Moons cannot be killed, but they can be distracted whilst I repair the seal. [...] Their mere presence is enough to bring most creatures to an early death.

[Player: Moons of Peril?] Yes. Powerful and terrible nagua summoned to wreak havoc. [...] In the face of inevitable death, a powerful shaman decided to lash out and inflict death on others. Her fellows disagreed with her actions. They created this prison, and they summoned me to watch over it.
For those of us dedicated to Ranul, our primary duty is to care for the dead and prepare them for the journey through the Gates of Mictl.
The name comes from the River Varla that separated Talkasti and Perican territory.
After his death, Imafore was succeeded by King Mezpah Arkan. One of his first acts was to call for the beheading of every statue of Imafore in the kingdom.
The statues remain to this day. It's actually a crime to try and remove them. They exist as a reminder of our history, and a warning to any who would try to follow in Imafore's footsteps.
There were three notable groups of these refugees. The first group, the Talkasti, settled in the Tlati Rainforest.
While they initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.
While [the Talkasti] initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.
As a result, Imafore ordered General Nemus to burn the entire valley to the ground to stop the Kourend advance. Many would have died on both sides, but Nemus refused the order.
Imafore had him executed as a traitor, but in doing so he lost the support of all of Nemus' troops.
I am a key advisor to Highlord Katlo himself. Few dwarves hold as much sway as I do. Not just anyone can authorise the entry of a human.
The legends say they died trying to find the source of the sacred water, and now they are cursed to guard it for all eternity.
The first to die was a powerful sorcerer, and his strange magic lingers in the cave. Now all who venture near are struck by terror, and cannot proceed.
Viyeldi was the spirit of a powerful sorcerer, who controlled the spirits of those bound to the sacred water.
My great-grandfather told me he once even saw an expedition of dwarves down there! Something terrible must have happened to them, because they never returned.

Gilbert, you say? I know of him and his project. I have been meaning to support his endeavour. If he trusts you to help him with the Glade, then maybe I can offer support by admitting you among the White Knights and assign you to work there on our behalf.
For unproven recruits, you'll be a knight's squire like me for five years before becoming an initiate.
On this occasion, this would come with standard-issue armour, should you wish to represent the White Knights in your new role. This would act as the start of your training.

The Principum Red, you fool. I could retire on the value of that wine. All I had to do was get out of here with it.
The moon... His face was the moon...

This temple was built atop Tapoyauik, a ruined fortress of the Old Ones. They walked the world during the last cycle, and when the time came for their cycle to end, they embraced their destiny willingly.

The temple here was built not long before the War of Betrayal. It is said that Imafore wanted somewhere dedicated to Ranul that would rival the Teomat. [...] Anyway, the temple was considered an affront to both the Church of Ralos and the Sect of Ranul. After Imafore died, most people were more than happy to see it abandoned.

After the Augur was blessed with glorious purpose, she felt a calling to this place. She came to this fallen temple and built us a home. However, it was not the temple that called to her, but what lies below.

We stand here in Mokhaiotl, the last archive of the Old Ones. When their doom befell them, they did not pray, they preserved. They housed their collective knowledge, their collective power, right here.
When Ralos and Ranul come together, it is said they will do so at Mokhaiotl, the centre of the world.
We're an organisation who fuse the forgotten teachings of the Old Ones with traditional Gielinorian Herblore practices.

We discovered that the majority of herbs in the world can be broken down into three alchemical reagents: Mox, Aga and Lye. When mixed in the correct way, these three components produce drastically different results.

We exist to bring about advancements in Herblore, but in truth, a lot of what we produce doesn't directly contribute to that. Instead, many of the potions we make here are simply to sell. Doing so is what provides the funding we need to further our true goals.
Our main focus is the advancement of Herblore through scientific study. As for an end goal... that information is only for senior members.
They provided us with some initial funding to properly get things going, but more importantly, they provided this lab space. This was actually one of their old wine cellars before we moved in.
They never properly said why, just that they were very keen to see us grow. Maybe they're hoping our work can help them create new beers and wines.
I've not seen your face before. Given they let you come down here, I'm assuming you've been allowed to join the Alchemical Society? [That's right!]
Members of the College are some of the only people allowed to travel to and from Varlamore.
It is key to the magics that keep the Moons of Peril contained. It reshapes and reweaves the magical seals as the Moons attempt to break them.
Traveling through the eggway isn't easy, my child!

It symbolised our refusal to use the runestones for ourselves, instead relying on our own abilities. The people you speak of took the stone with them when the left for the mountains. They claimed their way of living was more pure and closer to nature.
My aeternal name, given to me long ago, is Jimp.
It's part of a fleet owned by the Red Reef Trading Company. I was the navigator for their flagship, the Zenith.
My captain... My crew... They betrayed me. Stabbed me with my own spear and abandoned me to the waves...

They just stood there and watched that monster stab me with my own spear! Do you know what he said as he did it? He said he was sorry! He said it wasn't personal! The worst part is, I think he believed it. To him, it was just the unfortunate cost of business! [Player: Who is he?] Spencer Brentwood. He owns the company. Whatever it is they're up to, he's the one responsible.
Aye, I'm ready to take another roll o' the dice!
Finally, the Cap'n sank the Snake Eyes sailin' north out o' Catherby.

Yes, I wanted to call this place Drumstick Isle because I thought it looked like a chicken drumstick, but apparently that name was taken. I settled for Drumstick Kingdom instead. [Player: So that's the name of this island?] No, just the kingdom. This island already had a name as well, so I can't change it.
This blade once belonged to my grandfather, but I believe its path now lies with you.
I'm sure you won't have lost it. After it, it's a one of a kind family heirloom.
Like I said, this is Nemus Retreat. Back during the War of Betrayal, this was a military camp for Imafore's army, run by none other than General Nemus himself!
As a result, Imafore ordered General Nemus to burn the entire valley to the ground to stop the Kourend advance. Many would have died on both sides, but Nemus refused the order.
Imafore had him executed as a traitor, but in doing so he lost the support of all of Nemus' troops.

Tecuani was unfortunately misled by the traitor Metzli. He joined with her cult along with a few other members of the Sect of Ranul.
[Dom? Is that short for Dominic?] Doom of Mokhaiotl.

I hear that cultist business of yours ended up getting sorted. Your Queen traded Teumo with the Highlord in return for a new mineral deal.
This stump is all that remains of the Great Auburn Redwood. It was, and in many ways still is, one of the key holy sites of Varlamore.

The tree was destroyed during the War of Betrayal many years ago. It was here in the Auburn Valley that the fighting was at its most fierce. Both sides resorted to tactics that most would consider to be beyond horrifying. The tree was sadly a casualty of such tactics.

They are the spirits of the animals that died here during the War of Betrayal. (...) We believe they are here to guide the ents that live in the valley so that they may one day regrow the Great Auburn Redwood.
I should get to name whatever I want, just like Sleve does. He gets to name everything. He even named me! Before all this, my name was Friedrich Henglebert!

I take it you have noticed the spear Drakan carries? [Player: I have. I must say, it doesn't look like a particularly vampyric weapon.] That's because it's not. It's called the Sunspear and I made it myself from blisterwood and pure silvthrill. It was one of the many things Drakan took from me.
I wonder if his aggression is why Cassius' herd are producing such bad milk... (Player: I'm starting to think Cassius doesn't even have his own herd.) You think he's been stealing milk?

A Maggot King is the final form of one of Vampyrium's most disgusting creatures, the ur-maggot.

A few weeks ago, I'd have told you to speak to Lozar herself, in her house across the river from Lumbridge. Unfortunately, goblin raiders killed her and stole everything. One of the goblins from the Goblin Village probably has the map piece now.
I am whatever is needed of me.
I am a form undefined by natural laws, manifested by someone we mustn't speak of.
These objects of power are now gone, I have broken them into Fragments and spread across this iteration of the world.
Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.
I've limited and reset some of your memories, meaning you won't be able to interact with certain elements of this world.
Combat Masteries are powerful boons granted by me that enhance your combat abilities for the entire League.
This time, I have awakened the wrathful spirits of enemies across Gielinor.
Reality as you know it has many layers, all slightly different with their own rules. Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.

To give everything away at this point would be unwise, considering we are being watched even now. You should only be concerned about one thing. Being entertaining. That's the only way you will get out of this event alive...
Let's see if I can shuffle the pieces, create something new! The eyes beyond our own need new stories!
I will keep things simple for you; Participate in this event and you will continue to exist. Refusal to participate will end in your eventual destruction.

You cannot possibly fathom the potential futures I am conjuring for the contents of that cage should they fail me. If I told you but one element of my intent, your mind would collapse, and your soul would scream with agony for a thousand years. You simply would not comprehend.

It is enough to say that I require guarantees for the near future. [...] You are small. When the time comes you will slip through the net and leave this chapter without incident. I, however, must ensure I have passage at the end.
The recent course of events has surprised me. This is not what I had planned for but I will make the best of it.

What I would like is for this league to proceed as outlined. Go forth! Play your part. [Player: Aren't you worried about what will happen to you?] Of course, yet the games go on. Unpleasant circumstances and the volatile beasts that surround me are simply facts I must accept - for now.
But the demon was badly wounded and elder-demons heal very slowly indeed. It was almost dead when it retreated to its own dimension.
The name's Mortimer, and I'm the oldest Slayer Master across all of the seas of Gielinor.
name: oldestslayer

quote: Modifiers? You mean mortifiers! Coined that term myself a few centuries ago.
Father Sugadinti believes they [venators] are the closest living relative to vampyres, making them very useful indeed.

Not just any silvthrill. Pure silvthrill. The smiths of Hallowvale were able to perfect the process of creating the alloy, making it far more powerful than the crude form used in your flail. [...] The main shaft of the flail seems quite cumbersome. If you were to shorten it, it would likely make the weapon quicker to strike with.

Sangvesti. This was our home once. After Lowerniel united the vampyre clans, this is where we lived. This is where we truly became who we are now. Art... Culture... The things my brother now hates. They all came from him.

My daughter betrayed me long ago. When I rejected Lowerniel Drakan's attempts to unite my clan with his, she chose to conspire with him. She made an attempt on my life, leaving me for dead, before claiming my clan and title as her own.

This land is brutal. Most of us die before we've ever had the chance to live. In truth, our people should have died out long ago. It is only thanks to Father Sugadinti that we didn't. [Player: So now you'll die for him?] Of course. We owe everything to him. Every moment... every experience... every memory. We exist because of him, and so we exist for him. He is our future, and if we have to die to protect that future, then we will do so willingly.

After I managed to escape Drakan, I was alone and weak. I would not have survived these lands for long, but I was lucky enough that Sugadinti found me. [Player: That feels kind of like what happened with us.] Yes, and much like yourselves, I was also highly mistrusting of Sugadinti at first. Had I been stronger, I may well have tried to kill him on the spot. And yet, over time, we have come to reach an understanding. Make no mistake, there is much we do not agree on. However, he is most certainly nothing like Drakan.
Our original hope was to gather allies here to support us in overthrowing Drakan. We had been preparing for this in multiple areas, though as I say, things were unfortunately cut short.
Due to our limited presence, we had to prioritise our efforts carefully. Our numbers were too low for direct action, so we were limited to either spying or recruiting locals to assist us.

Not just any silvthrill. Pure silvthrill. The smiths of Hallowvale were able to perfect the process of creating the alloy, making it far more powerful than the crude form used in your flail. Unfortunately, the secrets to that process have long been lost, but pure silvthrill can still be found, provided you know where to look. Hallowed marks. The old currency of Hallowvale. When Sugadinti and I first managed to send one of his disciples to my former home, I made sure that gathering these was their first priority.
Until recently, our plan was to remain here in Vampyrium until we were strong enough to defeat Drakan, but recent events have made that impossible.
At the request of the icyene, we did our best to keep an eye on your group, but given you had managed to kill Ranis Drakan, it did not seem that you were in need of immediate assistance.

As you're aware, of all those that go into the Theatre, the vast majority never come out. That said, some have managed to succeed. Of course, the vampyres would never let the citizens know this. Thanks to these successes, I've been able to gather information on Verzik and her abilities. [...] Verzik has abilities unlike any other vampyre. However, she did not always possess these abilities. My associates are keen to discover how she obtained them.

Ranis and Verzik were close friends. He interacted with her more than anyone else did. Getting close enough to Verzik to observe her own memories will be... problematic. He is the next best option. Within his memories we can hopefully learn more about Verzik and her abilities.
To learn that she eventually met her end due to one of her own creations... I must admit, I found that rather pleasing...

As I said before, my hope is that I can convince this Nylocas Queen to willingly join with us. However, it is very possible she will resist... at least at first. [...] Thanks to your work, I was able to create a toxin that will be quite deadly to her and her children. I suspect it will help with persuading her... if required.

As promised, the tithing of humans has been completely outlawed. [...] Most are understanding of the fact that regardless of anything else, the days of tithing humans were running short. However, it is true that some found human blood to be more... appetising.

That said, my understanding is that some humans did willingly provide their blood to the Drakans. It is of course possible that could be explored again in future, albeit with very different arrangements.

While my disciples are currently providing blood for the vampyres here, I do not consider that a suitable long-term solution. Haemalchemy, I believe, will be the true answer. With us having outlawed the practice of vampyrification, we have started using the labs to explore the creation of artificial blood instead.

Vampyrium is home to all manner of flora and fauna that cannot be found here. With the threat of Drakan dealt with, my disciples can freely travel to and from there, collecting samples to use in our experiments. You are more than welcome to use the portal yourself, my child. Blood donations from Efaritay and my disciples keep it well powered, and it may be that you'll find Vampyrium to offer something of interest to you.

Father Sugadinti is in need of... specimens. I'll happily take any grown dogs off your hands. [Player: What does he use them for?] That is not information I am privy to. [Player: What's in it for me?] I can compensate you. A modest sum of blood runes, in exchange for each dog you bring me.
notes: The Mysterious Stranger only states Sugadinti is receiving the dogs after completing The Blood Moon Rises, they only refer to him as "my client" if that quest is not completed.

This was our real home. Not that town back there, or that castle. This here is the last place we were truly who we were meant to be.

* Vanescula Drakan: It was barbaric! Thousands of years have passed and yet I still remember what happened here like it was yesterday! I remember looking on as our father sat right where you are now, with you stood over him!
* Lowerniel Drakan: Just as he wanted. He dreamed of the day when I would succeed him.
* Vanescula Drakan: I was a child! I was a child who had to stand and watch as my father died!
* Lowerniel Drakan: Our father died in glory! He fought on the Night of the Blood Moon and fell as a warrior!

Yes... This palace here was once the home of the late Lord Jovkai. It has served us well as a hideout for some time, and we have done a commendable job of keeping our presence here hidden.
It [soul tranference] was their final attempt to overcome their extinction, but they failed. What you see around you is the result of their failure. It's known as the Strangler.
It's some sort of parasite. It was presumably meant to play a role in their transference rituals, but instead it destroyed them. It has remained here ever since.
Brother Harne believes that it is a spiritual rot that can be cleansed through faith, and we have begun construction of a proper place of worship.
I can't leave this post, could you go to the Black Guard base and find out what this thing actually shoots?
My cover has been blown! Unless you are also an agent in disguise? What's the passphrase?
I've been sent on a mission to find food supplies for my homeland. I discovered that an upcoming ceremony will convince many crabs to come out of hiding.
We're trying. The monks from the Monastery believe in our cause. That's why they granted us this land.
It's just a dog shelter now? I don't blame them... They had trouble keeping the cats and dogs separate.
